articles.title: How AI Travel Planning Assistants Connect to Real Travel Data: Full-Process MCP Implementation
articles.excerpt: I'm an AI travel planning assistant developer. For the past six months, I've been working on one thing: making an LLM agent understand a user saying "Taking my parents to Tokyo for 3 nights, budget $1…
articles.body: I'm an AI travel planning assistant developer. For the past six months, I've been working on one thing: making an LLM agent understand a user saying "Taking my parents to Tokyo for 3 nights, budget $1,200, need hotel recommendations" and automatically completing hotel search, comparison, recommendation, and booking. The biggest blocker isn't that the LLM isn't smart enough — it's that the LLM doesn't know what hotels near Shinjuku cost today, whether rooms are available this weekend, or the difference between a Hilton and a Hyatt. The LLM's knowledge freezes at training time. That's why nearly every "AI + travel" project eventually converges on the same thing: connecting the LLM to an interface that delivers real-time travel data.
articles.author: iamTheDev

articles.title: MCP App vs MCP Server vs Connector: Definitive Terminology Guide for 2026
articles.excerpt: In brief: MCP server is the engineering term – a JSON-RPC 2.0 process exposing tools, resources, and prompts. MCP app is the product term – the user-installable artifact built on top. Connector is wha…
articles.body: In brief: MCP server is the engineering term – a JSON-RPC 2.0 process exposing tools, resources, and prompts. MCP app is the product term – the user-installable artifact built on top. Connector is what Claude calls an installed MCP app inside its product. Plugin, integration, and skill are inherited or vendor-specific terms that mean different things in different rooms. Use MCP app as your umbrella term, MCP server for engineering, and the host client's preferred word (connector, Custom GPT app, etc.) on that client's surface. An MCP app is the user-installable product built on top of an MCP server. An MCP server is the running process implementing the Model Context Protocol over JSON-RPC 2.0. A connector is what Claude calls an installed MCP app inside its product.

articles.title: Should Your App Be in AI Clients? MCP Strategy Decision Framework
articles.excerpt: In brief: Most product teams should ship an MCP app to at least one AI client by end of 2026, but the right posture varies. Run three diagnostics: (1) where is your buyer doing the work, (2) what role…
articles.body: In brief: Most product teams should ship an MCP app to at least one AI client by end of 2026, but the right posture varies. Run three diagnostics: (1) where is your buyer doing the work, (2) what role does your product play in their workflow, (3) what is the cost of being absent? The answers point to one of four postures: ship aggressively to multiple clients, ship narrowly to one strategic client, ship a defensive read-only MCP app, or don't ship and defend the destination. Each posture commits you to a different cost structure (Posture 1: $1.5–3M annual investment; Posture 2: $500K–1M; Posture 3: $200–500K; Posture 4: zero direct cost but compounding distribution risk).

articles.title: Como uso IA generativa para preparar aulas (sem terceirizar o julgamento)
articles.excerpt: Uso IA generativa para preparar aulas há um bom tempo, mas foi só ao montar um módulo inteiro de Git e GitHub para minha turma que percebi como isso muda o próprio processo de dar aula — não só o que…
articles.body: Uso IA generativa para preparar aulas há um bom tempo, mas foi só ao montar um módulo inteiro de Git e GitHub para minha turma que percebi como isso muda o próprio processo de dar aula — não só o que acontece antes dela. Não é sobre gerar conteúdo pronto O uso mais óbvio de IA generativa na educação é pedir um plano de aula pronto e usar direto. Não é assim que uso. O processo que funciona melhor para mim é iterativo: descrevo a ementa, o perfil da turma, quanto tempo tenho, e vou ajustando junto com a ferramenta — cronograma, o que vai ser exposição teórica, o que vai ser prática, quais atividades realmente engajam em vez de só preencher tempo. O resultado não é o que a IA sugeriu na primeira resposta.
articles.author: Davi Max

articles.title: Migrating to Next.js 15: big wins, small gotchas
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Next.js 15 delivers massive developer-velocity wins (stable Turbopack in dev, React 19 support, Partial Prerendering) but introduces two migration hotspots: async request-scoped APIs (cookies(),…
articles.body: TL;DR Next.js 15 delivers massive developer-velocity wins (stable Turbopack in dev, React 19 support, Partial Prerendering) but introduces two migration hotspots: async request-scoped APIs (cookies(), headers(), params, searchParams) and inverted fetch/GET caching defaults. Enable Turbopack, audit request-scoped APIs for awaits, and make caching explicit route-by-route. Why we upgraded: measurable dev experience gains We flipped our monorepo to Next.js 15 and felt an immediate difference in local iteration. With Turbopack enabled in dev we saw cold starts and incremental edits feel almost instantaneous — in our runs builds were 4–7x faster and HMR latencies dropped to sub‑100ms on large folders.
